requirement_text: The prototype NE shall reside on a single commercial grade 6U VME board.
requirement_text_raw: The prototype NE shall (3.2.3.1.1.1) reside on a single commercial grade 6U VME board.
user_story: As a hardware engineer, I want the prototype NE to reside on a single commercial grade 6U VME board, so that it is built on standard hardware.
technical_task: Implement the prototype NE on one commercial grade 6U VME board.
acceptance_criteria: Given the prototype NE, when its hardware is inspected, then it resides on a single board.
Given the board, when its specification is checked, then it is a commercial grade 6U VME board.
rationale: Role assumed: hardware engineer.

requirement_text: Fault Tolerant System Services (FTSS) software shall use VxWorks Version 5.4 as the Operating System.
requirement_text_raw: Fault Tolerant System Services (FTSS) software shall (3.3.1.1) use VxWorks Version 5.4 as the Operating System.
user_story: As a software developer, I want FTSS software to use VxWorks Version 5.4 as the Operating System, so that the software runs on a known platform.
technical_task: Build and run the FTSS software on VxWorks Version 5.4 as the Operating System.
acceptance_criteria: Given the FTSS software, when it is built, then it targets VxWorks Version 5.4.
Given the FTSS software is running, when the Operating System is checked, then it is VxWorks Version 5.4.
rationale: Role assumed: software developer.

requirement_text: The system shall allow users to browse collections and view object and component details.
user_story: As a visitor, I want to browse collections and view object and component details, so that I can explore what is held.
technical_task: Provide pages to browse collections and view the details of objects and components.
acceptance_criteria: Given a list of collections, when the user browses them, then the collections are listed.
Given an object or component, when the user opens it, then its details are shown.
rationale: Role assumed: visitor.

requirement_text: User shall only delete routes that they have added.
user_story: As a user, I want to delete only the routes that I have added, so that I cannot remove other people's routes.
technical_task: Restrict route deletion to the user who added the route.
acceptance_criteria: Given a route added by the user, when the user deletes it, then the route is deleted.
Given a route added by another user, when the user tries to delete it, then the deletion is not allowed.
rationale: Role assumed: user.

requirement_text: The connection between the client and server shall have no more than 200ms latency.
user_story: As a user, I want the connection between the client and server to have no more than 200ms latency, so that the application responds promptly.
technical_task: Keep latency between the client and the server at or below 200ms.
acceptance_criteria: Given a client connected to the server, when latency is measured, then it is no more than 200ms.
Given a request from the client, when the server replies, then the round trip does not exceed the 200ms latency limit.
rationale: Role assumed: user. The second criterion treats latency as the delay of a request and reply, which is an interpretation.

requirement_text: The NE shall operate with a worst case card edge thermal interface temperature of +65 °C for greater than 10 hours.
requirement_text_raw: The NE shall (3.2.3.1.3.1.2) operate with a worst case card edge thermal interface temperature of +65 °C for greater than 10 hours.
user_story: As a hardware engineer, I want the NE to operate at a worst case card edge thermal interface temperature of +65 °C for greater than 10 hours, so that it keeps working in hot conditions.
technical_task: Verify that the NE operates with a worst case card edge thermal interface temperature of +65 °C for greater than 10 hours.
acceptance_criteria: Given the card edge thermal interface is at +65 °C, when the NE runs for greater than 10 hours, then it continues to operate.
Given the NE is tested at the worst case temperature, when the test ends, then the NE has operated throughout the period.
rationale: Role assumed: hardware engineer. The unit symbol in the source text is garbled and read as degrees Celsius.

requirement_text: Performance requirements The capability of the computer depends on the performance of the software. The software can take any number of inputs provided the database size is larger enough. This would depend on the available memory space.
rationale: The text describes performance in general terms ("any number of inputs", "available memory space") without a testable requirement.
clarification_questions: What performance targets (response time, throughput) are required?
How large is the database and what memory is available?

requirement_text: The event is logged (UC 5 S8) and the HCP is returned in the specific office visit record to verify his or her changes.
requirement_text_raw: The event is logged (UC 5  S8) and the HCP is returned in the specific office visit record to verify his or her changes.
user_story: As an HCP, I want the event to be logged and the specific office visit record to show my changes, so that I can verify them.
technical_task: Log the event and return the HCP to the specific office visit record so the HCP can verify the changes.
acceptance_criteria: Given an HCP has made changes, when the changes are saved, then the event is logged.
Given the event has been logged, when the HCP is returned to the office visit record, then the HCP can see the changes to verify them.
rationale: The reference to (UC 5 S8) is context only; the behaviour is the logging and the return to the record.

requirement_text: The solution should provide the ability to use digital signatures as the means for attestation.
user_story: As a clinician, I want to use digital signatures for attestation, so that attestations are signed.
technical_task: Support digital signatures as the means of attestation.
acceptance_criteria: Given a record that needs attestation, when the user attests it, then a digital signature is applied.
Given an attested record, when it is viewed, then it shows that it was attested with a digital signature.
rationale: Role assumed: clinician.

requirement_text: System shall comply with relevant privacy regulations and standards to safeguard user privacy and data security.
rationale: "Relevant" regulations and standards are not named, so compliance cannot be tested.
clarification_questions: Which privacy regulations and standards apply?
How is compliance to be verified?

requirement_text: This decision shall be made based on the health and status of all the physical links from the FCP to the CTC.
requirement_text_raw: This decision shall (3.4.2.7) be made based on the health and status of all the physical links from the FCP to the CTC.
user_story: As a system operator, I want the decision to be based on the health and status of all physical links from the FCP to the CTC, so that decisions reflect the state of the links.
technical_task: Base the decision on the health and status of all the physical links from the FCP to the CTC.
acceptance_criteria: Given the physical links from the FCP to the CTC, when the decision is made, then the health and status of all of them is considered.
Given one physical link has a poor status, when the decision is made, then that status is taken into account.
rationale: Role assumed: system operator. The decision itself is not described in this sentence.

requirement_text: User shall be able to log in to Gmail using their email id and password.
user_story: As a Gmail user, I want to log in with my email id and password, so that I can access my account.
technical_task: Implement login to Gmail using an email id and password.
acceptance_criteria: Given a registered email id and its password, when the user logs in, then the user is signed in.
Given a wrong password, when the user tries to log in, then the login is refused.
rationale: Role assumed: Gmail user.

requirement_text: System shall ensure data security and privacy by encrypting emails and implementing robust authentication mechanisms.
user_story: As an email user, I want my emails encrypted and protected by authentication mechanisms, so that my data stays private and secure.
technical_task: Encrypt emails and implement authentication mechanisms for access.
acceptance_criteria: Given an email, when it is stored or sent, then it is encrypted.
Given a user who is not authenticated, when the user tries to access emails, then access is denied.
rationale: Role assumed: email user. "Robust" is not measurable, so the criteria cover only encryption and authentication.

requirement_text: Users will be able to turn the sound on or off at any stage during the game.
user_story: As a player, I want to turn the sound on or off at any stage of the game, so that I can control the audio.
technical_task: Provide a control to switch game sound on or off during any stage of the game.
acceptance_criteria: Given a game in progress, when the player turns the sound off, then the sound stops.
Given the sound is off, when the player turns it on at any stage, then the sound plays again.
rationale: Role assumed: player.

requirement_text: System shall be able to display an enlarged version of the main site image when the user clicks on it on the sites page.
user_story: As a visitor, I want to click the main site image on the sites page to see an enlarged version, so that I can see it in more detail.
technical_task: Display an enlarged version of the main site image when the user clicks it on the sites page.
acceptance_criteria: Given the sites page, when the user clicks the main site image, then an enlarged version of the image is displayed.
Given an enlarged image is shown, when the user closes it, then the sites page is shown again.
rationale: Role assumed: visitor. The closing behaviour is an assumption.

requirement_text: On each FCP, the FTPP system shall configure the Radstone firmware to perform the IBIT tests shown in Table 3.3.2.1, FCP IBIT Table.
requirement_text_raw: On each FCP, the FTPP system shall (3.3.2.26) configure the Radstone firmware to perform the IBIT tests shown in Table 3.3.2.1, FCP IBIT Table.
user_story: As a system integrator, I want the FTPP system to configure the Radstone firmware on each FCP to perform the IBIT tests, so that the tests in Table 3.3.2.1 are run.
technical_task: Configure the Radstone firmware on each FCP so it performs the IBIT tests listed in Table 3.3.2.1, FCP IBIT Table.
acceptance_criteria: Given an FCP, when the FTPP system configures it, then the Radstone firmware is set to perform the IBIT tests.
Given the IBIT tests are configured, when they are compared with Table 3.3.2.1, then they are the tests shown in that table.
rationale: Role assumed: system integrator. The contents of the table are not given.

requirement_text: The LHCP chooses to view a report of all patients of a single or either gender in a specified age range with none one or more diagnoses.
requirement_text_raw: The LHCP chooses to view a report of all patients of a single or either gender  in a specified age range   with none  one  or more diagnoses.
user_story: As an LHCP, I want to view a report of patients of a chosen gender within a specified age range and with zero or more diagnoses, so that I can review a patient group.
technical_task: Generate a report of patients filtered by gender (single or either), a specified age range and any number of diagnoses.
acceptance_criteria: Given the report options, when the LHCP selects a gender, an age range and diagnoses, then the report lists patients matching the selection.
Given the LHCP selects either gender, when the report is run, then patients of both genders are included.
rationale: Role stated: LHCP. "None one or more diagnoses" is read as zero, one or more diagnoses.

requirement_text: User shall be able to use only well-visible buttons.
rationale: "Well-visible" is subjective and not measurable.
clarification_questions: Should the visibility be judged against a contrast or size criterion?

requirement_text: User shall have ALFRED preinstalled, eliminating the need for manual setup.
user_story: As a user, I want ALFRED to be preinstalled, so that I don't need to set it up manually.
technical_task: Deliver the system with ALFRED already installed.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new user receives the system, when it is first used, then ALFRED is already installed.
Given the delivered system, when the user starts it, then no manual setup of ALFRED is required.
rationale: Role assumed: user.

requirement_text: The system should efficiently handle medium-sized information databases without significant performance degradation.
rationale: "Medium-sized", "efficiently" and "significant" are not defined.
clarification_questions: How large is a "medium-sized" information database?

requirement_text: User shall navigate back to the previous screen using the back button located in the top left corner of every screen except the Homepage.
user_story: As a user, I want a back button in the top left corner of every screen except the Homepage, so that I can return to the previous screen.
technical_task: Add a back button in the top left corner of every screen except the Homepage that navigates to the previous screen.
acceptance_criteria: Given any screen other than the Homepage, when the user views it, then a back button is shown in the top left corner.
Given the back button is shown, when the user selects it, then the previous screen is displayed.
Given the Homepage, when the user views it, then no back button is shown.
rationale: Role assumed: user.

requirement_text: User shall be able to use the system without experiencing any faults, even with a high number of items and users.
rationale: "Any faults" and "a high number" are not quantified, so the requirement cannot be tested.
clarification_questions: How many items and users count as "a high number"?
What fault rate, if any, is acceptable?

requirement_text: Clicking 'Edit' next to one of these sections will present you with this patient's issues list for that category.
user_story: As a clinician, I want to click Edit next to a section to see the patient's issues list for that category, so that I can review the issues.
technical_task: Show the patient's issues list for a category when the user clicks Edit next to that section.
acceptance_criteria: Given a section of the patient record, when the user clicks Edit next to it, then the patient's issues list for that category is shown.
Given the issues list is shown, when the user views it, then it contains only the issues for the selected category.
rationale: Role assumed: clinician. The second criterion follows from "for that category".

requirement_text: The system shall render complex projects faster with a compatible graphics card.
user_story: As a designer, I want complex projects to render faster with a compatible graphics card, so that I spend less time waiting.
technical_task: Use a compatible graphics card to speed up rendering of complex projects.
acceptance_criteria: Given a complex project and a compatible graphics card, when the project is rendered, then rendering uses the graphics card.
Given the same project with and without a compatible graphics card, when both are rendered, then the render with the card is faster.
rationale: Role assumed: designer. "Faster" is relative; no time target is given.

requirement_text: The system shall be configurable to prevent corruption or loss of data already accepted into the system in the event of a system failure (e.g. integrating with a UPS etc.).
requirement_text_raw: The system shall be configurable to prevent corruption or loss of data already accepted into the system in the event of a system failure (e.g. integrating with a UPS  etc.).
user_story: As a system administrator, I want the system to be configurable to prevent corruption or loss of accepted data in a system failure, so that data stays safe.
technical_task: Make the system configurable so data already accepted is protected from corruption or loss in the event of a system failure, for example by integrating with a UPS.
acceptance_criteria: Given the system configured for failure protection, when a system failure occurs, then data already accepted into the system is not corrupted.
Given the same configuration, when a system failure occurs, then data already accepted into the system is not lost.
rationale: Role assumed: system administrator. The UPS is given only as an example.

requirement_text: User shall view and select available examination categories.
user_story: As a candidate, I want to view and select available examination categories, so that I can choose my exam.
technical_task: Display the available examination categories and let the user select one.
acceptance_criteria: Given available examination categories, when the user opens the examination page, then the categories are listed.
Given the list of categories, when the user selects one, then that category is chosen.
rationale: Role assumed: candidate.

requirement_text: FTSS shall only allow a single task residing on each specified virtual group to "open" the respective end of the pipe.
requirement_text_raw: FTSS shall [SRS230] only allow a single task residing on each specified virtual group to "open" the respective end of the pipe.
user_story: As a software developer, I want FTSS to allow only a single task on each specified virtual group to open its end of a pipe, so that pipe ends have one owner.
technical_task: Allow only one task residing on a specified virtual group to open the respective end of the pipe.
acceptance_criteria: Given a pipe end in a specified virtual group, when a single task opens it, then the open succeeds.
Given a pipe end already opened by a task in that virtual group, when a second task tries to open the same end, then the open is not allowed.
rationale: Role assumed: software developer.

requirement_text: The Clinical Task Assignment & Routing capability should provide non-repudiation requirements (IN 1.5) that guarantees that the sources and receivers of data cannot deny that they entered or sent or received the data.
user_story: As a clinician, I want sources and receivers of data not to be able to deny entering, sending or receiving it, so that data exchange can be trusted.
technical_task: Provide non-repudiation (IN 1.5) in the Clinical Task Assignment & Routing capability for entering, sending and receiving data.
acceptance_criteria: Given data is entered or sent, when the action completes, then a record shows the source cannot deny it.
Given data is received, when the receipt completes, then a record shows the receiver cannot deny it.
rationale: Role assumed: clinician. The mechanism for non-repudiation is not stated.

requirement_text: A maximum of 10 Free Users shall be allowed in Webble with limited access to features.
user_story: As a product owner, I want a maximum of 10 Free Users in Webble with limited access to features, so that free use is capped.
technical_task: Limit Webble to a maximum of 10 Free Users and restrict their access to features.
acceptance_criteria: Given 10 Free Users exist, when an 11th Free User tries to register, then the registration is refused.
Given a Free User, when the user opens a feature outside the limited access, then the feature is not available.
rationale: Role assumed: product owner. The 11th user in the first criterion follows from the maximum of 10.

requirement_text: The FTSS API shall specify a memory map that provides the boundaries for congruent aligned memory, congruent initialized memory, and non-congruent memory.
requirement_text_raw: 2.     The FTSS API shall [SRS217] specify a memory map that provides the boundaries for congruent aligned memory, congruent initialized memory, and non-congruent memory.
user_story: As a software developer, I want the FTSS API to specify a memory map, so that I know the boundaries of congruent aligned, congruent initialized and non-congruent memory.
technical_task: Specify in the FTSS API a memory map giving the boundaries for congruent aligned memory, congruent initialized memory and non-congruent memory.
acceptance_criteria: Given the FTSS API specification, when a developer reads it, then it contains a memory map.
Given the memory map, when a developer reads it, then it gives the boundaries for congruent aligned, congruent initialized and non-congruent memory.
rationale: Role assumed: software developer.

requirement_text: System shall never include unauthorized records in search results.
user_story: As a user, I want search results never to include unauthorized records, so that I only see what I may access.
technical_task: Filter search results by the user's authorization so unauthorized records are excluded.
acceptance_criteria: Given records the user is not authorized to see, when the user searches, then those records are not in the results.
Given records the user is authorized to see, when the user searches, then matching records are in the results.
rationale: Role assumed: user.

requirement_text: To add one of these clearinghouses click on 'X12 Partners' and then click the 'Add New Partner' button.
requirement_text_raw: To add one of these clearinghouses  click on 'X12 Partners' and then click the 'Add New Partner' button.
rationale: The sentence reads as help text for using the screen; it states no system behaviour to implement.
clarification_questions: Is this a requirement or a user instruction?
What must the system do when a partner is added?

requirement_text: The solution should require that the new prescription label be barcode-checked before the product can be dispensed.
user_story: As a pharmacist, I want the new prescription label to be barcode-checked before the product is dispensed, so that the right product goes out.
technical_task: Require a barcode check of the new prescription label before a product can be dispensed.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new prescription label that has not been barcode-checked, when dispensing is attempted, then it is not allowed.
Given a new prescription label that has been barcode-checked, when dispensing is attempted, then it is allowed.
rationale: Role assumed: pharmacist.

requirement_text: The solution should conform to Auditable Records to audit all changes to privilege rules.
user_story: As a compliance officer, I want all changes to privilege rules audited, so that changes can be traced.
technical_task: Record an auditable entry for every change to privilege rules, conforming to Auditable Records.
acceptance_criteria: Given a privilege rule, when it is changed, then an auditable record of the change is created.
Given the audit records, when a reviewer opens them, then the changes to privilege rules can be found.
rationale: Role assumed: compliance officer.

requirement_text: All computers within the CMCS system shall have the ability for authorized users to directly access individual systems for maintenance and monitoring through remote logins.
user_story: As a system administrator, I want authorized users to log in remotely to individual CMCS computers, so that I can maintain and monitor them.
technical_task: Enable remote logins for authorized users to directly access individual CMCS computers for maintenance and monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Given an authorized user, when the user logs in remotely to a CMCS computer, then the user can access that computer.
Given a user who is not authorized, when the user tries a remote login, then access is refused.
rationale: Role assumed: system administrator.

requirement_text: System shall ensure data security and compliance with relevant regulations and standards.
rationale: The regulations and standards are not named, so compliance cannot be tested.
clarification_questions: What data security measures are expected?

requirement_text: User shall be able to initiate the investigation process for registered complaints.
user_story: As an officer, I want to start the investigation process for a registered complaint, so that the complaint is investigated.
technical_task: Allow users to initiate the investigation process for registered complaints.
acceptance_criteria: Given a registered complaint, when the user initiates the investigation process, then the investigation starts.
Given a complaint that is not registered, when the user tries to initiate an investigation, then the investigation does not start.
rationale: Role assumed: officer. The second criterion follows from "registered".

requirement_text: The product shall make the users want to use it. 80% of the users surveyed report they are regularly using the product after the first 2 weeks post-launch.
requirement_text_raw: The product shall make the users want to use it. 80\% of the users surveyed report they are regularly using the product after the first 2 weeks post-launch.'
user_story: As a product owner, I want 80% of surveyed users to report regularly using the product after the first 2 weeks post-launch, so that the product is engaging.
technical_task: Run a survey of users after the first 2 weeks post-launch and check that 80% report regularly using the product.
acceptance_criteria: Given users surveyed after the first 2 weeks post-launch, when the results are counted, then 80% report regularly using the product.
Given the survey results, when fewer than 80% report regular use, then the requirement is not met.
rationale: Role assumed: product owner. The sample size is not given.

requirement_text: The SQL database must have scalable capacity.
user_story: As a database administrator, I want the SQL database to have scalable capacity, so that it can grow with the data.
technical_task: Configure the SQL database so its capacity can be scaled.
acceptance_criteria: Given the SQL database is running, when more capacity is needed, then the capacity can be increased.
Given capacity is increased, when the database is used, then existing data remains available.
rationale: Role assumed: database administrator. The scale target is not given.

requirement_text: System shall secure in-app purchases via encryption and use a reliable payment gateway.
user_story: As a customer, I want in-app purchases to be secured by encryption through a reliable payment gateway, so that my payment is protected.
technical_task: Encrypt in-app purchases and process them through a reliable payment gateway.
acceptance_criteria: Given a customer makes an in-app purchase, when payment details are sent, then they are encrypted.
Given an in-app purchase, when the payment is processed, then it goes through the payment gateway.
rationale: Role assumed: customer. "Reliable" is not measurable.

requirement_text: You may click on an issue in the list at any time to edit it.
user_story: As a clinician, I want to click an issue in the list at any time to edit it, so that I can keep the list current.
technical_task: Allow any issue in the list to be opened for editing by clicking it at any time.
acceptance_criteria: Given a list of issues, when the user clicks an issue, then the issue opens for editing.
Given an issue being edited, when the user saves it, then the updated issue appears in the list.
rationale: Role assumed: clinician.

requirement_text: The system shall display "video not found" if the requested video is not available.
user_story: As a viewer, I want to see "video not found" when the requested video is unavailable, so that I know why nothing plays.
technical_task: Display the message "video not found" when the requested video is not available.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requested video that is not available, when the user requests it, then "video not found" is displayed.
Given a requested video that is available, when the user requests it, then "video not found" is not displayed.
rationale: Role assumed: viewer.

requirement_text: User shall be able to navigate through the CCTNS application.
user_story: As a police officer, I want to navigate through the CCTNS application, so that I can reach the functions I need.
technical_task: Provide navigation through the CCTNS application.
acceptance_criteria: Given the CCTNS application is open, when the user selects a navigation item, then the related page is displayed.
Given a page in the application, when the user navigates to another, then the user can return to the first page.
rationale: Role assumed: police officer. The pages and functions are not listed.

requirement_text: The system shall allow applicants to satisfy hearing requirements before a hearing.
user_story: As an applicant, I want to satisfy hearing requirements before a hearing, so that I am ready for the hearing.
technical_task: Allow applicants to complete the hearing requirements before the hearing date.
acceptance_criteria: Given a scheduled hearing, when the applicant completes the hearing requirements before the hearing, then the requirements are recorded as satisfied.
Given an applicant who has not completed the requirements, when the hearing is reviewed, then the unmet requirements are shown.
rationale: Role stated: applicant. The hearing requirements themselves are not described.

requirement_text: A server shall host the Swiggy App and provide system data processing and storage capability.
user_story: As a product owner, I want a server to host the Swiggy App and provide data processing and storage, so that the app has a backend.
technical_task: Provision a server that hosts the Swiggy App and provides system data processing and storage.
acceptance_criteria: Given the Swiggy App, when it is deployed, then it is hosted on a server.
Given data from the app, when it is processed and stored, then the server provides the processing and storage capability.
rationale: Role assumed: product owner.

requirement_text: System shall have a contractual agreement with an internet service provider for T3 access with 99.9999% availability.
user_story: As an operations manager, I want a contractual agreement with an internet service provider for T3 access with 99.9999% availability, so that connectivity is covered.
technical_task: Obtain a contractual agreement with an internet service provider for T3 access with 99.9999% availability.
acceptance_criteria: Given the service provider contract, when it is reviewed, then it covers T3 access.
Given the service provider contract, when its availability terms are reviewed, then they state 99.9999% availability.
rationale: Role assumed: operations manager.

requirement_text: System design shall prioritize modularity to facilitate efficient maintenance.
user_story: As a maintenance engineer, I want the system designed to be modular, so that maintenance is efficient.
technical_task: Structure the system design into modules so that each part can be maintained separately.
acceptance_criteria: Given the system design, when it is reviewed, then it is divided into modules.
Given a change to one module, when it is made, then other modules need little or no change.
rationale: Role assumed: maintenance engineer. "Efficient" is not measured; the criteria look at module structure.

requirement_text: The system shall be able to handle large and complex spreadsheets without significant performance degradation.
rationale: "Large", "complex" and "significant" are not defined.
clarification_questions: What size counts as "large" and "complex" for a spreadsheet?

requirement_text: System shall facilitate smooth registration for summits.
rationale: "Smooth" is subjective and no registration behaviour is described.
clarification_questions: What does "smooth" mean for summit registration?

requirement_text: The system shall have basic data integrity checking to reduce the possibility of incorrect or invalid data being introduced.
requirement_text_raw: The system shall have basic data integrity checking to reduce the possibility of incorrect or invalid data being introduced.'
user_story: As a data steward, I want basic data integrity checking, so that incorrect or invalid data is less likely to be introduced.
technical_task: Add basic integrity checks that reject incorrect or invalid data on entry.
acceptance_criteria: Given invalid data is entered, when the system checks it, then the data is not accepted.
Given valid data is entered, when the system checks it, then the data is accepted.
rationale: Role assumed: data steward. "Basic" checks are not listed.
